dedupe_keys.name: food safety inspection model netlogo models of inspector search strategies in a food safety system three variants

description: The Food Safety Inspection Model represents a very basic food safety system in which inspectors, consumers and stores interact. It was written in NetLogo by Sara McPhee-Knowles and published in the CoMSES library as three separate codebases (2014, updated 2019), one for each search strategy of the inspectors: a random strategy, one in which stores close when consumers stop visiting them, and one in which stores can signal a problem to inspectors and consumers, with or without errors. Food products and suppliers are assumed to be part of the stores. The purpose is to give insight into the right number of inspectors for a food system. All three versions are available as free downloads from CoMSES under the AFL-3.0 licence. Caveats: the system is abstract, with no real inspection data. Coverage is general. Simulation uses: sizing inspection services and comparing inspection strategies for retail food. Related records: the food supply chain structure model for China (model-comses-food-supply-chain-structure-china) also includes a food safety regulator as an agent.
inputs: Inspector search strategy (random, store closure, store signalling)
name: Food Safety Inspection Model: NetLogo models of inspector search strategies in a food safety system (three variants)
outputs: Detection of problems in stores and the level of inspection needed
